body:
Research swept vision and found one dominant candidate plus three ranked smaller ones. Shipped the top candidate; recording the rest.

SHIPPED. SwinBlock.windowedAttention per-window per-head loop was about 95% of the package backend dispatches for about 2% of its arithmetic: roughly ten Execute calls on 256-element tensors per (window, head) pair, each an output allocation plus an Attrs interface box. Seven of the ten are pure data movement or elementwise scaling (three column slices, one transpose, the inverse-sqrt scale, the relative-bias add, the mask add) plus two levels of Concat. The fused arm does all of that as index arithmetic over packed storage and keeps only Q-Kt, the softmax, and weights-V. Scattering each head output directly into the destination IS both Concat levels. Gated on ctx.Recorder == nil because scratch reuse is unsafe under a tape.

Measured, median of 8 runs at 50 iterations, Apple M2 Pro darwin/arm64: block wmsa -9.23 percent time, -24.64 percent bytes, -73.22 percent allocations; block swmsa -10.41 percent, -74.06 percent allocations; whole model batched -6.10 percent and -69.18 percent allocations; per-image -3.38 percent and -53.88 percent allocations.

A NEW BENCHMARK WAS REQUIRED FIRST. BenchmarkSwinForwardBatched dilutes this loop about 5x behind the projection and MLP GEMMs, so a genuine win reads there as noise; BenchmarkSwinBlockForward isolates one block on the same token grid.

KEY CORRECTNESS FINDING, now rule SEPARATE-STATEMENTS-DO-NOT-STOP-FMA-001 and folded into perfscan PS3025: writing the scale/bias/mask chain as three separate STATEMENTS does not prevent FMA contraction. The Go spec permits fusing across statements; arm64 contracted the pair and diverged from the dispatched path on 66 of 256 logits. Only an explicit conversion per step forces the rounding, and in generic code the conversion to the type parameter, T(x*s), does work. The exact-equality gate caught this; a tolerance gate would not have.

NOT TAKEN, with reasons. (a) Per-block loop invariants rebuilt every Forward (swinBuildMasks, headBias, the index permutations) are cacheable and bit-identical, but swinBuildMasks runs once per batched Forward and headBias is 18 calls of 12.5k MACs, so under 1 percent batched and 3 to 5 percent per-image. Worth folding in later, not on its own. (b) vision/mae.go unshuffleRows and gatherRows do a Slice per row plus one Concat where swinGather already shows the one-op row-gather idiom; bit-identical, but NO benchmark exists for MAE at all, so it is unsizable until Reconstruct or MAELoss gets one. (c) ViT and MLPMixer batched paths are already fully jammed; their remaining loops are B=8 scaffolding against large GEMMs, and the time is in nn/backend. (d) patchify variants do per-element closure dispatch through makeReader plus a wasted float64 intermediate on the F32 path, real but 24.6k reads against 240M MACs. (e) perfscan PS1005 at swin.go:921 and 14 PS6016 hits are constructor-time or once-per-Forward; PS4011 hits are batch fan-outs, not decode recurrences. (f) scaleInPlace re-fetches storage inside its loop but is constructor-only.
